title: Trump Lands in Beijing for High-Stakes Summit With Xi Jinping
excerpt: Trade, Taiwan, and the Iran war dominate as the first US presidential visit to China in nearly a decade gets underway
body:
US President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing on Tuesday for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping that could reshape the trajectory of the world's most consequential bilateral relationship. It is the first visit by an American president to China since 2017.

The two-day meeting, scheduled for May 14-15, comes against a volatile backdrop: an ongoing US-led military campaign against Iran, spiraling oil prices that have crossed $104 a barrel, and a fragile trade truce that has paused but not resolved the tariff war between the world's two largest economies. Tech titans Elon Musk and Apple CEO Tim Cook are part of the American delegation, signaling that technology and AI governance will feature prominently alongside traditional security concerns.

**The Iran Factor:** Washington wants Beijing to use its leverage with Tehran to broker a ceasefire in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's naval blockade has disrupted global shipping lanes and sent energy markets into turmoil. China, which imports roughly half its crude oil from the Middle East, has its own reasons to want stability — but Xi is expected to extract concessions on semiconductor restrictions and Taiwan in exchange for any diplomatic assistance on Iran.

**Trade and Technology:** The 90-day tariff truce agreed in Geneva last week reduced US duties on Chinese goods from 145 percent to 30 percent, providing temporary relief. But unresolved disputes over rare earth export controls, AI chip restrictions, and Chinese electric vehicle subsidies loom large. Beijing has signaled willingness to discuss energy purchases and market access for American agricultural products, though analysts caution that structural disagreements on industrial policy remain deep.

**Taiwan's Shadow:** The summit occurs weeks after China conducted its largest military exercises near Taiwan in two years. Trump has sent mixed signals on Taiwan — alternately describing Xi as a friend and warning of consequences for any military action. Taipei is watching nervously; any grand bargain that trades reduced Taiwan support for Chinese cooperation on Iran would send shockwaves through the Indo-Pacific.

For the Indian-American community, the summit's outcomes carry direct economic consequences. The US-China trade relationship shapes global supply chains that Indian IT services companies navigate daily. A breakdown in talks could accelerate the decoupling that has already redirected some manufacturing to India, while a deal on rare earths could ease chip shortages affecting Indian tech startups. India's diplomatic establishment, meanwhile, watches any US-China rapprochement warily — a warmer Washington-Beijing axis could dilute the Quad's strategic momentum.

**What to Watch:** Markets will parse every communique for signals on tariffs, Taiwan language, and any Iran mediation framework. The yuan's movement against the dollar and any announcements on semiconductor trade will be the first concrete indicators of whether substance matched spectacle.
nri_angle: US-China trade dynamics directly affect Indian IT supply chains and manufacturing shifts to India, while any strategic rapprochement could reshape the Quad alliance that underpins Indo-Pacific security.
